lead.headline: Sensex falls about 1,000 points as Brent tops $102 and US bond yields hit multi-year highs
lead.short: At 13:25 the Sensex was at 71,670, down 968 points, and the Nifty at 22,261, down 1.5%; about ₹8.5 lakh crore of market value was gone. Brent rose another 2% to above $102 after the most attacks on Hormuz tankers in a single week since the war began, and the US 10-year yield passed 5.3%. ITC, Adani Ports, IndiGo and Reliance led the fall; IT shares rose before TCS reports this evening.
more: Foreign investors have sold for nine straight sessions, nearly ₹57,000 crore, and were net sellers on 20 of 25 days since September began. Analysts read Wednesday's change of RBI stance as the bigger signal than the rise itself: Jefferies expects about 100 basis points of rises in this cycle.

why.text: Dearer oil and dearer money at once: both reach the household budget, and the market is pricing more rate rises to come.

update.new: The biggest fall in weeks, on oil above $102, US yields and the RBI's new stance.
update.front: A 1,000-point fall with oil above $102 is the day's money news on its own.

seconds.headline: Nana Patekar dies at 75 at his home in Goa
seconds.short: The actor died of a suspected cardiac arrest, PTI reported; three hours earlier he had texted a friend that he was not feeling well. In nearly five decades of Hindi and Marathi films, from Gaman in 1978 to Parinda, Krantiveer and Salaam Bombay!, he won three National Film Awards and the Padma Shri. Prime Minister Modi praised his "intensity, individuality".

why.text: One of the few actors whose anger on screen felt real, and a farmer's champion off it.

seconds.headline: Three more FIRs against Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi, this time for assaulting police; the CEC's security is raised
seconds.short: The cases, from Wednesday's second day of protests, are for assault on police, obstructing government work and manhandling officers. Rahul Gandhi, detained again, said: "Every FIR is a medal on my chest... Right now, there are 45, my goal is 100." Security at Gyanesh Kumar's home and office has been increased as the INDIA bloc steps up its campaign.
seconds.highlight: Every FIR is a medal on my chest

why.text: The standoff is hardening into criminal cases on one side and more protests on the other.

update.new: Three FIRs for assaulting police after a second day of protests; security raised for the CEC.
update.front: The opposition leader now faces assault charges over the protest; that escalates the story on its own.

seconds.headline: GPT-6 reaches ChatGPT, free users included, with answers that can carry charts, maps and buttons
seconds.short: Paying users get GPT-6 Sol from Wednesday; Free and Go users start getting the smaller GPT-6 Luna from Thursday. The headline feature, Intelligent UI, lets ChatGPT answer with charts, forms, maps, tappable buttons or small working tools when they suit the question, and plain text when they do not. OpenAI says web-search answers come 44% faster.

why.text: The first time OpenAI's newest family reaches the free tier, and a change in what a chatbot answer looks like.

seconds.headline: US proposes a $70,000 fee for each foreign student who works after graduating
seconds.byline: DHS · HIGHER ED DIVE · FOX NEWS · 7 OCT
seconds.short: The Department of Homeland Security wants universities to pay $70,000 per student for initial Optional Practical Training and $30,000 for each later period, including the STEM extension; they could pass it on to students or employers. It is a proposal, open to comment for 30 days, and its legal basis is already disputed.

why.text: Indians are the biggest group of foreign students in the US, and OPT is how most of them get their first job there.

briefs.headline: PNB, Bank of Baroda, Bank of India and Indian Bank pass on the rate rise to repo-linked loans
briefs.text: PNB's repo-linked rate goes to 8.35% from 8.10% and Bank of India's to 8.35%, Indian Bank's to 8.20% and Bank of Baroda's retail rate to 8.15%, all from 7 or 8 October.

update.new: Banks raised their repo-linked lending rates.
update.front: The rate rise has reached actual loan rates at four big banks; that is a change for borrowers today.

briefs.headline: The UPI merchant fee due on 15 October may be pushed to January
briefs.text: Reuters reports officials are weighing a delay to give payment firms time and spare merchants a change during the festive season; NPCI has not decided. Payments to people stay free either way.

update.new: The start date may move from 15 October to January.
update.front: A charge due in a week may not come; that changes what merchants plan for the festive season.

briefs.headline: Mbappé expected to be fit for Villarreal, though Mourinho may save him for Roma
briefs.text: Reports say his knee has recovered in time for Saturday; Madrid play at Roma in the Champions League next week, and the Clásico is later this month.

update.new: He is expected to be fit for Saturday.

data.max_note: He has never won in Singapore; his best there is three second places.

preview.text: Marina Bay is slow, bumpy and hot: braking, traction and rear grip out of tight corners decide it, overtaking is hard, so qualifying and the safety car matter. Mercedes call it a stronghold, but their Sepang upgrade made the car slower in low-speed corners, and Singapore is where they will find out why. Verstappen arrives from his first win of the year, his third straight top-two finish.
preview.favours: Traditionally Mercedes; any car with strong traction out of slow corners

picks.says: Singapore's slow corners are the real test of whether Mercedes' upgrade misfired or Sepang's surface was to blame.
Antonelli expects answers on the upgrade before Singapore, another traditional Mercedes stronghold.

briefs.headline: FIA finds the Sepang stall was a software bug in the wet-weather power cut, and changes the rule for Singapore
briefs.text: Cars at low revs in sectors where power was cut to 250kW lost more than intended and could not recover it; a further software update follows. Singapore is also declared a heat-hazard race, so drivers may wear cooling vests.

update.new: The FIA published its findings on the stall at the start.

briefs.text: The strikes hit Abha and King Khalid International in Riyadh, injuring 36; the Ministry of External Affairs condemned the targeting of civilian infrastructure.

update.new: Houthi attacks on Saudi airports killed three.

briefs.text: The communications ministry says all three licensed satellite firms are at the same stage, waiting on security checks before they can seek spectrum.

briefs.headline: Chemistry Nobel to Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai for reactions that make one mirror-image form of a molecule
briefs.text: Life uses only one 'hand' of many molecules, and drugs often must too; their work helped chemists make the right one.

briefs.text: The order applies to all child custody cases in the state's courts.

screen.reason: Indian critics found Iñárritu's oil-rig satire bold and rewarding, British and American ones laboured and smug; nearly all say Cruise's self-mocking turn is the reason to go.

screen.title: Drishyam: The Conclusion
screen.reason: A satisfying close to the franchise: Devgn's silent Vijay and Jaideep Ahlawat's cop carry it, though critics differ on how much the slow first half and the courtroom twists cost it.

screen.title: Verity
screen.reason: Most critics found the Colleen Hoover thriller silly and unconvincing, wasting Anne Hathaway and Dakota Johnson; a few enjoyed it as knowing camp.

screen.title: Resident Evil
screen.reason: Zach Cregger's reboot is gory, fast and often funny, with Austin Abrams a likeable lead; its critics say the chaos outruns any real dread.

screen.title: Heart of the Beast
screen.reason: An old-fashioned man-and-dog survival story in Alaska, lifted by Brad Pitt and the dog; reviews run from deeply moving to serviceable.

screen.title: The Uprising
screen.reason: Andrew Garfield is committed and the battle scenes hit hard, but most critics found Paul Greengrass's Peasants' Revolt epic thin, grim and flat.

screen.title: Mirzapur: The Movie
screen.reason: Fan service done well: Pankaj Tripathi's Kaleen Bhaiya and the dialogue carry it, though almost every critic says its 197 minutes sag in the second half.
